name: agentavow-trust

tools.name: scan_repo
tools.description: Scan a public GitHub repo ('owner/name') for a signed 0-100 trust score and a plain safe / needs-review verdict before connecting.

tools.name: scan_package
tools.description: Scan a published npm / PyPI / crates / Docker / Hugging Face package for a signed 0-100 trust score and a safe / needs-review verdict.

registry.description: npm | pypi | crates | docker | huggingface (aliases like python/rust/hf accepted).

tools.name: scan_mcp_server
tools.description: Scan a live MCP server by its https URL — checks the tool definitions for poisoning / prompt-injection — signed verdict.

tools.name: verify_trust
tools.description: Resolve an agent identity and return its current trust score before you delegate to it.

tools.name: check_interaction_safety
tools.description: Check whether it's safe to perform a given interaction (delegate/trade/…) with an agent.

tools.name: lookup_identity
tools.description: Resolve a DID (did:web:… / did:key:…) or search agents by name.

tools.name: get_trust_badge
tools.description: Get a shields-style trust badge (SVG URL + README markdown) for an agent identity.

tools.name: about_agentavow
tools.description: What AgentAvow checks, which tool to use for what, and how to read a verdict.

instructions: AgentAvow — the "is this safe to connect?" layer for AI agents. Point it at a GitHub repo, an npm/PyPI/crates/Docker/Hugging Face package, a live MCP server, or an agent identity and get a signed 0-100 trust score, a plain safe / needs-review verdict, the findings behind it, and certified eligibility. Every result is Ed25519/JWS-signed and recomputable offline. Read-only, no account. This is the local/stdio build of the same service as the remote connector at https://agentavow.com/mcp.
